_comment: THIS FILE IS THE SOURCE OF TRUTH for vault-research, the way
vault-claude-settings.json is for vault-claude. install-settings.sh
materialises it into <scratch>/.claude/settings.json on every start, so
edit it here, push, deploy. A hand-edited copy is overwritten unless
VAULT_SETTINGS_MANAGED=0. DECISIONS.md#a-third-surface-for-research.
WHAT THIS AGENT IS. A Claude Code session with web search and web fetch,
rooted in a scratch volume that is NOT the vault and does not contain it.
It researches, downloads, and writes its findings where vault-claude can
read them. vault-claude then files what is worth keeping. Two sessions,
one direction, and the vault is only ever on the far side.
WHY THE DENY LIST HERE IS SHORTER THAN VAULT-CLAUDE'S, AND WHY THAT IS
NOT A RELAXATION. The two files break DIFFERENT legs of the same risk.
Prompt injection needs private data, untrusted content and a way out.
vault-claude has the first two and is denied the third: it reads the whole
vault and cannot send. This agent has the last two and is denied the first:
it can search and fetch the open web, and there is nothing of yours in the
room. Do not 'harmonise' these two files. Making this one look like that
one would take away the web tools that are the entire point; making that
one look like this one would hand the vault an exfiltration channel. The
asymmetry is the design. ARCHITECTURE.md#trust-boundary.
THE WORKING DIRECTORY IS THE SECURITY BOUNDARY, not the deny list below.
research.sh starts Claude Code with cwd set to the scratch root, and the
vault is not mounted into this container at all. The denies that matter
here cover what IS reachable: this agent's own credentials, and the files
that define its behaviour.
The //vault, //snapshots and //backups denies are therefore rules for paths
that do not exist, kept on purpose as a tripwire. Someone will eventually
add a mount to this service to make one task easier, and these turn that into an
agent that cannot read what it just gained rather than one that silently
can. They cost nothing while the mounts are absent. If you find yourself
deleting them to make something work, that is the review, not the fix.
//backups is the one worth naming: it holds the bundles, which are the
whole vault, and AGE_RECIPIENT ships empty so they are plaintext by
default. research.sh refuses to start if it finds that mount.
NO HOOKS. vault-claude commits the vault around every session and stamps
the notes it writes. Neither applies here: the scratch volume is not a git
repo and is not meant to be, and nothing this agent writes is a vault note
yet. The record of what it did is the audit log from fetch_attachment and
whatever vault-claude files afterwards, which IS stamped and committed.
PATH SYNTAX. A single leading slash anchors at the SETTINGS SOURCE, which
for this file is the scratch root, not the filesystem root. Absolute paths
take '//'. Path rules are consulted for Read and Edit only; Write(path) is
accepted and never checked. Both mistakes are silent. This is the same trap
that left /snapshots undefended in vault-claude's policy for three weeks --
DECISIONS.md#the-snapshots-deny-that-was-not-one -- and preflight.sh now
asserts against both files.
BASH IS DENIED, and here the reason is different from vault-claude's. There
it is denied because it is the way out. Here there is already a way out, so
denying it buys something narrower and still worth having: no arbitrary
process on the NAS's network, and no reading of files this policy has not
considered. curl and wget would also route around fetch_attachment's
checks -- the private-address guard, the size cap, the type sniffing --
and land whatever they liked on disk. See ../vault-mcp/fetch.go.
AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md are WRITE-DENIED at any depth, for the reason they
are in the vault: Claude Code reads them as standing instructions, and this
agent reads attacker-authored web pages all day. A fetched page that talks
the agent into appending to CLAUDE.md turns one bad afternoon into every
future session. Reading them is allowed; the agent needs its instructions.
Edit them from the repo, never through the agent.
.claude/ and .mcp.json are denied the same way and for the stronger reason:
an entry in .mcp.json is a command every future session executes, which is
the persistent compromise above with the shell this policy just removed.
READING A FETCHED FILE IS DENIED, and this is the rule that makes the
quarantine claim in ../vault-mcp/fetch.go true of the SURFACE rather than
only of the tool. fetch_attachment hands back a name, a size and a type and
never the bytes -- but Claude Code's Read tool DOES open images and PDFs and
present them to the model, so without these denies the agent could simply
Read the file it had just downloaded, one turn later. A downloaded image is
attacker-controlled content that can carry rendered text; the whole point of
keeping it out of a model's context is lost if another tool lets it back in.
The extensions here are fetchableTypes in ../vault-mcp/fetch.go and must not
drift from it: a type this agent can fetch but not read is safe, a type it
can fetch and read is the hole. Denying Read also blocks Edit and Write on
the same paths, which is fine -- nothing here should be editing a PNG.
WEBFETCH IS UNRESTRICTED BY DOMAIN, deliberately. A domain allowlist does
not survive contact with real research -- every new topic is a new list --
and the control doing the work here is what this session can READ, not
where it can reach. FETCH_ALLOW_HOSTS in .env can narrow fetch_attachment
for a deployment that wants both. DECISIONS.md#a-third-surface-for-research.
CLAUDE.AI CONNECTORS ARE OFF, and on this surface that is not a tidiness
measure. Claude Code logged into a claude.ai subscription fetches that
account's connectors and serves them as MCP tools, and the account here is
the same one that owns the vault. On 2026-09-05 this agent was found
holding Gmail, Google Drive, Notion, Deep WIKI and kylejs Obsidian Vault,
which is the vault-mcp connector: read AND write access to the notes, in
the one container built to contain nothing of yours, beside WebSearch and
WebFetch.
Every claim above about this surface assumed the mounts were the boundary.
They are the boundary for the FILESYSTEM. A connector needs no mount: it
is an outbound HTTPS call from this process to Anthropic's bridge, so the
tripwire in research.sh, the missing vault volume and every //vault deny
in this file were all looking the wrong way. The comment above that says
'there is nothing of yours in the room' was false while a connector was
loaded, and is true again only with this key set.
TOP LEVEL, beside env, not inside permissions. 'true' from any scope wins.
docker-compose.yml sets ENABLE_CLAUDEAI_MCP_SERVERS=false for the same
effect from the environment, so the guarantee does not rest on this file
having been installed. The setting covers connectors Claude Code fetches
for itself, which is this case; it does not cover a desktop app or cloud
host delivering them in-process. Confirm with /mcp in a live session:
vault-tools should be the only server. https://code.claude.com/docs/en/mcp
enabledMcpjsonServers pre-approves vault-tools because the project-MCP
trust prompt has no one to answer it at container start.
